comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body: Workaround found: `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` (pinning the review to the reviewing worktree's own HEAD instead of the default `origin/main` attested snapshot) avoids the foreign-HEAD stale-head failure entirely — confirmed on epic 759e-7dc1-675c-4877, which then produced a clean content-based BLOCK/PASS cycle with no further stale-head symptom. This is consistent with the working hypothesis in the description: whatever internal mechanism backs the default `source=attested, ref=origin/main` path is where the foreign-commit contamination happens; pinning `--ref` to a value that doesn't require that shared attested-checkout machinery sidesteps it. Left open — the root cause in the attested/origin-main path is still unfixed and will still bite any ticket that doesn't pass `--ref HEAD` explicitly.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RCA (runtime-confirmed) — foreign `stale-head` from the unscoped whole-HEAD currency read

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** The unscoped whole-HEAD "fail-safe" currency arm violates its own
contract: it must decide whether the *reviewed code* has moved since review (anchored to the
signed gate-ref sha), but instead reads `git rev-parse HEAD` of whatever working tree the
evaluator sits in and compares that against a gate-ref anchor.

### Mechanism (proven at runtime, DEBUG-rebar-debug instrumentation)

`compute_validity` unscoped arm, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:655-663`:
```
elif manifest_file_scope(auth_manifest) != "none":
    head = signing.head_sha(_config.repo_root(repo_root))   # git rev-parse HEAD of a working tree
    signed_head = _authoritative_head(attestation)          # for attested opcert = merged_log_commit = verified_at_sha = GATE-REF sha
    if head == "unknown" or signed_head != head:
        return _result(False, ..., "stale-head")
```
For an **attested** opcert, `_authoritative_head` (attest.py:398-410) returns `merged_log_commit`,
which `_opcert_signing.py:372` sets to `verified_at_sha` — the **gate-ref (origin/main) sha at
review time**. So the check compares a *gate-ref* sha against a *working-tree branch HEAD*. They
match only by luck (a fetched main-tracking checkout). Any other tree — a feature-branch worktree,
the long-lived MCP server's own cwd, or a `git rev-parse HEAD` that walks UP out of a no-`.git`
attested-snapshot dir into a foreign enclosing repo — yields a spurious, **foreign** `stale-head`.

Because both the gate-ref anchor and the foreign tree's HEAD are stable, the foreign value is
**identical across invocations** (matches the ticket's two-reads-15-min-apart evidence: a
stuck/foreign read, not a live race). origin/main having NOT moved is exactly why the review is
genuinely fresh yet still rejected.

**Runtime evidence** (targeted repro, gate ref G unmoved, working tree diverged to feature F):
```
gate ref origin/main (G)          = 440a34c6fb8dc0c73bce0e7137cdf879d0aa4d17
working-tree HEAD    (F)          = 32a8985e892377fa31486441e31daeb254a07a47   (foreign to gate ref)
signed_head (_authoritative_head) = 440a34c6...   (== G, the signed gate-ref anchor)
head_sha read from repo_root      = .../repo   ->  returned 32a8985e...  (== F)
compute_validity verdict          = 'stale-head'  valid=False
reason: attestation is stale (unscoped; signed at 440a34c6..., HEAD is 32a8985e...)
```
Confirmed: the currency check certified against G, then read the *working tree* F, not the gate
ref — a false `stale-head` while G is unmoved.

### Root cause / attribution (`caused_by`, date-tested)

- `3040aa0c` (2026-06-24, epic `boil-golem-veto` S1) introduced this unscoped whole-HEAD check.
  It was **correct then**: pre-attested-snapshots, the *signed* side was also the working-tree
  `head_sha`, so both sides were the same tree — symmetric, no defect.
- **`ill-hazel-probe` (`30b3-b001-4ee2-43d2`, epic `raze-vet-ditch` S4, 2026-06-27)** made
  `verified_at_sha` the signed anchor — a **gate-ref sha** — for attested opcerts, but did **not**
  update this unscoped whole-HEAD *current* read to resolve the gate ref. That change **created
  the asymmetry** (gate-ref signed side vs working-tree current side). → **true origin / unmet
  obligation.** `0c1d0c18` (2026-07-21) only re-touched adjacent lines (pin-validity) — a carrier,
  not the origin.
- Siblings `piney-gold-day` (S4b) / `72d9` / `505d` fixed the **scoped** path to re-hash at the
  current gate ref (ADR 0002, `gate_ref_hash_basis`, fail-closed) but never migrated the
  **unscoped** whole-HEAD path — this is the missed consumer. (505d is DISTINCT: it fixes the
  scoped path failing OPEN; this bug is the unscoped path failing CLOSED with a foreign value.)

### Fix scope (respects the ticket non-goal)

Mirror the already-shipped scoped-path pattern: in the unscoped whole-HEAD arm, when the manifest
carries a `verified_at_sha` (attested), resolve the **current gate-ref sha** locally
(`resolve_ref(default_ref, repo_root, fetch=False)`) and compare to the signed `verified_at_sha`;
fail **closed honestly** ("cannot confirm gate ref") if unresolvable — never a foreign value.
Legacy opcerts with no `verified_at_sha` keep the `head_sha` read unchanged. This **preserves the
whole-HEAD invalidation granularity/semantics** (still whole-origin/main, still fails closed on a
genuinely moved gate ref) and corrects only the wrong VALUE read — squarely within the ticket's
declared non-goal (do NOT change invalidation granularity).

comments.body:
PARITY SWEEP (Step 7) — complete. Swept every unscoped-HEAD / head_sha / rev-parse HEAD currency read for the same 'gate-ref anchor vs working-tree HEAD basis mismatch' defect:

FIXED (this work): (1) attest._unscoped_head_drift [plan-review, #2399 core + #2401 shared helper]; (2) drift_floor code_drifted [plan-review Pass-3 finding-drop, #2401].

CORRECT-by-design, NOT parity defects: (3) transition_close.py:401 completion drift guard — the COMPLETION gate pins its default target to HEAD via _pin_completion_ref (ref is None -> resolve_ref('HEAD')), so its verified_at_sha basis IS the working-tree HEAD, matching the close-time head_sha(working) read. Same-basis comparison; no foreign read. This is the KEY asymmetry: plan-review's default gate ref is origin/main (gate-ref basis), completion's is HEAD (working-tree basis). (4) _opcert_signing.py:372/407 — the signing/anchor-SETTING side (records the anchor), correct by design. (5) relation_snapshot.tracker_head_sha — reads the TRACKER (tickets branch) HEAD, a different domain (not code gate-ref currency).

SIBLING 505d-b2c5 ('Claim gate fails OPEN when the current gate ref cannot be resolved: _hash_basis silently substitutes the working tree') — confirmed DISTINCT and left untouched (in_progress under another session): it fails OPEN (substitutes working tree) in a different function (_hash_basis); 1137 fails CLOSED with a foreign value. Not merged, per the non-goal. Note: my shared helper current_head_sha fails CLOSED (raises SnapshotError) on an unresolvable attested gate ref — orthogonal to and non-conflicting with 505d's _hash_basis surface.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Running `rebar review-plan` on epic `759e-7dc1-675c-4877` (compliant-lemon-grunion, an epic with no `file_impact`, so it falls to the `CURRENCY_BASIS_FAIL_SAFE` / unscoped-whole-HEAD path in `attest.py:648-663`) produces a PASS verdict, but signing then fails with `stale-head`: the "current HEAD" reported does not match the code repo's real state.

Concretely: `rebar ls-remote origin main` and `rebar ls-remote gerrit main` both confirm the real, current `main` tip is `4dafd36d2aa1f0e264634392698a1a4ba952c70b` — matching `verified_at_sha` in the attestation. But the `stale-head` error reports the "current HEAD" as `f1dd41a8f09967dd60c7aefb5e43c6f62fa119af`, a commit titled "Diagnose MCP client PAT wiring in doctor" that:

- exists as a git object (`git cat-file -t f1dd41a8... ` → `commit`) — so it is reachable in the shared object store — but
- is not the tip of `origin/main`, `gerrit/main`, nor the reviewing worktree's own branch/HEAD (`compliant-lemon-grunion-impl`, confirmed at `9a94ef9737fb` throughout, via `git reflog`).

This value was **identical across two independent `review-plan` invocations ~15 minutes apart** (different `signed_at` timestamps, same reported "HEAD"), which rules out an ordinary live race (a live race would show a *different*, more-recent HEAD each retry as `main` continued to move) and instead points at a **stuck/foreign value being read**, not a genuinely fresh git query against the reviewing worktree.

`attest.py`'s `stale-head` path calls `signing.head_sha(_config.repo_root(repo_root))`, where `head_sha` (`src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py:202`) runs `git -C <repo_root> rev-parse HEAD`. `_config.repo_root(None)` resolves, in order, `explicit arg > REBAR_ROOT env > git toplevel of cwd` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:74`). `REBAR_ROOT` was confirmed unset in the reviewing shell and in `~/.zshrc`/`~/.zprofile`/`~/.bashrc`/`~/.bash_profile`. The reviewing worktree's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` should return its own linked-worktree root, so `repo_root` should resolve correctly to the reviewing worktree — yet the returned HEAD belongs to neither that worktree nor either remote's main.

Working hypothesis (unconfirmed — needs a maintainer with instrumentation access): the attested-mode review path may use an internal temporary checkout/worktree to pin `ref=origin/main` for the review, and that temp path may not be uniquely namespaced per invocation. On a host running ~90 concurrent agent worktrees (confirmed via `git worktree list` at the time of this report) each independently running `rebar review-plan`, two concurrent invocations could collide on a shared temp-checkout path, leaving one invocation's HEAD-freshness check reading another invocation's (or another ticket's) checked-out commit.

## Impact

An epic-level (or any ticket with no scoped `file_impact`) plan-review can PASS its content review yet permanently fail to sign under concurrent multi-agent load, because the currency check races against unrelated concurrent reviews rather than the reviewing worktree's own state. This blocks `claim` (directly, and via the parent-claim cascade for every child ticket) with no available remediation path other than the disallowed `--force`.

## Reproduction

1. On a host running many concurrent `git worktree`-based rebar checkouts, each with active agent sessions.
2. From one worktree, run `rebar review-plan <epic-id>` on an epic with no `file_impact` (forces the unscoped/fail-safe currency path).
3. Review computes and signs a PASS, but the sign step's freshness check reports a `stale-head` error whose "current HEAD" does not match `git rev-parse HEAD` in the reviewing worktree, nor `origin/main`, nor `gerrit/main`.
4. Retry immediately: the SAME foreign HEAD value is reported again (not a newer one), indicating a stuck/foreign read rather than a live race against `main` continuing to move.

## Scope (proposed, needs confirmation by whoever picks this up)

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (the `stale-head` currency check, `CURRENCY_BASIS_FAIL_SAFE` path)
- Whatever attested-mode temp-checkout mechanism backs `source=attested` review (not yet located in this investigation — needs tracing from the review entry point through to wherever an attested snapshot's local checkout path is constructed)
- `src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py::head_sha` (confirm whether `repo_root` passed to it is ever something other than the reviewing worktree's cwd-derived root)

## Non-goals

Fixing the underlying "unscoped whole-HEAD invalidation is a blunt/racy proxy" design tension (that's a legitimate design choice per `drift_floor.py`'s own docs) — this bug is specifically about the HEAD VALUE READ being wrong/foreign, not about whether whole-HEAD invalidation is the right granularity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For an attested manifest (`verified_at_sha` present), the unscoped whole-HEAD currency arm resolves the CURRENT gate ref locally (`resolve_ref(default_ref, repo_root, fetch=False)`) and compares it to the signed `verified_at_sha`, instead of reading `git rev-parse HEAD` of the evaluator working tree.
- [ ] A currency check certified at an UNMOVED `origin/main` gate ref stays `valid` when evaluated from a foreign working-tree HEAD (no spurious `stale-head`); proven by `test_attested_unscoped_head_freshness_reads_gate_ref_not_working_tree`.
- [ ] The check STILL returns `stale-head` when the gate ref genuinely moves (invalidation granularity/semantics preserved); proven by `test_attested_unscoped_head_freshness_still_invalidates_on_moved_gate_ref`.
- [ ] Legacy opcerts with no `verified_at_sha` keep the existing `head_sha` read unchanged (no behavior change); covered by `test_signed_empty_scope_head_drift_contract`.
- [ ] An unresolvable gate ref fails CLOSED honestly ("cannot confirm gate ref"), never emitting a foreign value.
- [ ] Module size stays <=800 LOC and the complexity ratchet passes with no baseline bump: checked via `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.

## Testing / Verification

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` -- the RED->GREEN oracle (positive + negative control) plus the legacy contract test all pass.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` run clean.
- Mutation check: seeding the root-cause `head = head_sha(working)` back into the attested branch makes the positive oracle go RED (mutant killed), confirming the test has teeth.

file_impact.reason: Add current_head_sha(auth_manifest, repo_root) shared helper: the SINGLE source of the unscoped current-head anchor. Attested -> resolve the current gate ref (resolve_ref/default_ref, fetch=False); legacy/source=local -> head_sha. Raises SnapshotError on an unresolvable attested gate ref (fail closed, no foreign value).

Refactor _unscoped_head_drift to delegate to gate_source.current_head_sha instead of git rev-parse HEAD of the evaluator working tree; catch SnapshotError -> fail-closed reason; legacy/source=local keep the head_sha read via the shared helper.

code_drifted (Pass-3 finding-drop eligibility) sourced the byte-identical unscoped head_sha read; route it through the shared gate_source.current_head_sha so the two intentionally-synchronized anchors cannot diverge; catch SnapshotError -> unknown (deny convergence, never suppress).

RED->GREEN oracle: attested unscoped attestation certified at an unmoved origin/main gate ref stays valid from a foreign working-tree HEAD (positive), still stale-head when the gate ref genuinely moves (negative control), plus a shared-helper real-store test for current_head_sha.
Teeth tests for the drift_floor consumer: the candidate reads the shared gate-ref anchor not the working tree, and denies convergence (never suppresses) when the gate ref is unresolvable.
